For manufacturers and sourcing teams, the speech signals focus on skilling, apprenticeships, ITI upgrades and ease of doing

title: Philippines’ T&A imports decline but exports grow in Jan-Jul
summary:
Philippines’ textile and apparel imports fell 6.05 per cent year on year to $1.288 billion in January–July 2026 as textile input purchases declined, though apparel imports edged up.
Exports rose 3.17 per cent to $599.30 million as yarn and fabric shipments rose 15.36 per cent, offsetting lower apparel exports; July imports fell 10.04 per cent and exports 13.44 per cent.

title: CITI seeks India-US talks over 100% tariff law signed by Trump
summary:
India’s CITI has warned that possible US tariffs under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 could affect textile and apparel exports. 
The body said MSME-led exporters may struggle to absorb extra duties in the US, their largest market. 
It urged closer India-US engagement, a balanced trade deal and cautioned that FTAs cannot quickly replace US demand.

title: Euro area current account surplus falls to $32.2 bn in July
summary:
Euro area current account surplus narrowed to €28 billion (~$32.2 billion) in July 2026 from a month earlier, ECB data showed. 
The month’s balance rested on a €36 billion goods surplus and €12 billion services surplus, offset by income deficits. 
Over 12 months, the surplus fell to 1.7 per cent of GDP as the goods surplus declined, relevant for textile and apparel teams tracking EU trade demand.

title: Trump signs law as India risks 100% tariffs over Russian oil
summary:
US President Donald Trump has signed H.R. 5334, expanding sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions on Russia and extending existing sanctions on Iran. 
The law can expose goods from top Russian oil and gas buyers, including India and China, to duties of up to 100 per cent. 
Importers and sourcing teams face possible tariff changes within 30 days of signing.

title: EU businesses redesign supply chains amid geopolitical risks
summary:
EU businesses are redesigning supply chains as geopolitical risks become a structural feature of global trade, an EIB-European Commission study finds. 
While 64 per cent of firms feel prepared, trade obstacles are shifting from raw materials and logistics to tariffs and regulatory compliance. 
Supply-chain adjustments also fell, while firms invest in diversification and resilience.

title: India's FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7% on economic resilience: Moody’s
summary:
Moody’s Ratings has raised its forecast for India’s real GDP growth in FY2026-27 to 7 per cent from 6 per cent, citing stronger-than-expected economic momentum and resilience to global disruptions. 
Growth is being supported by private consumption, infrastructure investment and sustained services activity. 
Moody’s maintained a stable outlook on India’s Baa3 sovereign rating.

title: Germany’s industries face fresh pressure from increasing energy costs
summary:
Germany’s industrial producer prices rose 4.6 per cent YoY in August 2026 and 1.1 per cent from July, signalling higher domestic cost pressure.
Energy climbed 8.3 per cent and intermediate goods 6.1 per cent, key inputs for manufacturing and sourcing budgets.
Excluding energy, producer prices rose 3.1 per cent YoY and 0.2 per cent MoM.

title: India’s trade gains face new tariff uncertainty
summary:
New Zealand’s Parliament has passed legislation to implement the India FTA, with all Indian goods to receive duty-free access after ratification.
For Indian textiles, apparel and made-ups, removing 5-10 per cent duties could improve price competitiveness in New Zealand.
A US sanctions bill could allow tariffs of up to 100 per cent on Russian energy buyers, adding risk to India-US trade talks.

title: Netherlands’ unemployment rises to 408,000 in August: CBS
summary:
Netherlands had 408,000 unemployed people in August 2026, up by an average of 3,000 a month over three months, according to the CBS. 
Paid employment fell by an average of 1,000 a month; employed people have hovered around 9.8 million for almost three years. 
UWV benefit recipients rose 1.4 per cent month on month to 194,800, a labour signal for sourcing and retail teams.

title: Beyond power cuts: What’s at stake for Bangladesh’s RMG sector?
summary:
BKMEA survey shows Bangladesh knitwear factories face severe energy disruption, with 90 per cent citing electricity shortages and 75 per cent hit by gas crisis. 
Knitting output fell around 37–38 per cent, sewing about 40 per cent and dyeing 51 per cent; 87 per cent reported shipment delays. 
Higher fuel costs, buyer discounts, order cuts and loan-default risks are also rising.

title: Vietnam targets $48 billion textile-garment exports in 2026
summary:
Vietnam targets about $48 billion in textile-garment exports in 2026; eight-month shipments rose 2.9 per cent YoY to nearly $31.7 billion. 
Exporters face a 12.5 per cent US tariff, higher costs, fabric delays and uneven order cover for the final months. 
Firms are prioritising higher-value orders, market diversification, digitalisation, input control and ESG compliance.

title: UK’s clothing exports fall to $314 mn in July 2026
summary:
The United Kingdom's clothing exports fell 5.62 per cent year on year to £235 million in July 2026 but rose from £229 million in June.
Textile fabric exports dropped 4.95 per cent to £211 million; fibre exports were £46 million, above July 2025 but below June.
In Q2 2026, clothing exports eased 1.93 per cent to £711 million, while 2025 exports declined 9.17 per cent to £3,013 million.

title: Gen Z, millennial parents are Carter's new target in refresh
summary:
Carter's is pushing deeper into kidswear with a new logo and Watch Them Glow campaign to keep families beyond babywear.
US babywear imports fell to $784 million in January-June 2026 from $944.9 million a year earlier, Texpro data shows.
Gap, Kohl's and Abercrombie are also targeting children's apparel, as Carter's leans on stores and Walmart, Target and Amazon distribution.

title: Bangladesh's garment exports to EU fall 13.65% in January-July 2026
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment exports to the European Union fell 13.65 per cent year on year to €10.37 billion in January-July 2026, significantly exceeding the EU’s overall 5.10 per cent decline in garment imports. 
China and Vietnam recorded export growth during the period, while Bangladesh also saw lower shipment volumes and average export prices.

title: India apparel exports slide 11% as $6.5 bn sourcing prize emerges
summary:
India’s apparel retail market is estimated at ₹9.3 lakh crore in FY25 and projected at ₹16 lakh crore by FY30, with organised retail at about 41 per cent.
TexPro shows 2025 exports still below 2015 levels; H1 2026 exports fell 11.2 per cent, while imports rose 13.3 per cent.
Nearly 2,000 planned fashion-store openings could create about $6.5 billion in additional garment and allied sourcing.

title: New ₹2,000 UPI rule tests ₹27,000-cr apparel payment market
summary:
From October 15, qualifying UPI purchases above ₹2,000 incur a 0.4 per cent merchant fee; customers pay no surcharge.
Apparel is close to the cut-off: August 2026 average UPI tickets were ₹886 at family-clothing shops and ₹1,195 at men's and women's stores.
India's apparel exports fell 11.2 per cent in H1 2026; festive period contributes nearly 35 per cent of annual apparel sales.

title: South Korean apparel imports rise 2.8% in January-August 2026
summary:
South Korea’s apparel imports rose 2.82 per cent to $7.901 billion in January-August 2026, with August shipments up 10.98 per cent to $1,283.819 million.
Knitted apparel imports grew 4.64 per cent and non-knitted apparel imports rose 1.47 per cent in the first eight months.
Exports of man-made filaments fell 4.32 per cent, while knitted or crocheted fabrics gained 8.56 per cent.

title: Is mono-fabric design changing the future of waterproof outerwear?
summary:
BAM launched the Any Weather Mac in September 2026, describing it as the UK’s first certified-recyclable waterproof coat.
The coat uses mono-fabric construction, about 90-95 per cent recycled polyester, a virgin CoPES membrane and a removable zinc-alloy zip head.
It has a PFAS-free finish, 10,000mm rating, welded seams, take-back route and Infinitee certification.

title: US’ Gap Inc appoints Kirsten Green to board of directors
summary:
Gap Inc has appointed Forerunner founder and managing partner Kirsten Green to its board of directors with immediate effect.
Green brings venture investment experience in consumer-led growth, scaling brands and anticipating shifts in customer behaviour.
The move supports Gap Inc’s transformation as it strengthens core apparel businesses and expands brand reach into beauty and accessories.
